question: Amit invests a sum of ₹5400 and Gopal invests a sum of ₹10200 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 4 years, Gopal gets ₹960 more interest than Amit, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in Principal = ₹10200 − ₹5400 = ₹4800

Simple interest generated by extra principal in 4 years = ₹960

Simple interest for 1 year = 960 ÷ 4 = ₹240

Rate of Interest (R) = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Extra Principal) × 100

R = (240 ÷ 4800) × 100 = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal invested by Amit (P₁) = ₹5400

Principal invested by Gopal (P₂) = ₹10200

Time (T) = 4 years

Difference in Simple Interest = ₹960

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Difference in SI = [(P₂ − P₁) × R × T] ÷ 100

 
 Amit: ₹5400
 
 ₹5400
 
 Diff: ₹4800
 Gopal: Total ₹10200
 

 

 SI Diff = ₹960
 Time = 4 yrs

**Calculations:**

⇒ Difference in SI = [(10200 − 5400) × R × 4] ÷ 100

⇒ 960 = [4800 × R × 4] ÷ 100

⇒ 960 = 48 × R × 4

⇒ 960 = 192 × R

⇒ R = 960 ÷ 192

⇒ R = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate of Interest, and T is Time.

Difference in Interest for Same Time & Rate

When T and R are constant, the difference in Simple Interest is directly proportional to the difference in Principal: ΔSI = (ΔP × R × T) ÷ 100.

Compound Interest vs Simple Interest

For the first year, SI and CI are equal if compounded annually. For subsequent years, CI is calculated on the accumulated interest as well, making CI greater than SI.
